projects.title: Feature-Engineered MRI Classification of FCD
projects.summary: I built this multimodal neuroimaging pipeline after becoming interested in how subtle epilepsy-related abnormalities can remain invisible during standard MRI review. The project explored whether interpretable structural MRI features could still capture measurable group-level differences between patients with focal cortical dysplasia and healthy controls using machine learning.
projects.description:
This project focused on building an interpretable multimodal MRI analysis pipeline for detecting structural patterns associated with focal cortical dysplasia (FCD), one of the most common causes of drug-resistant epilepsy. Using the OpenNeuro ds004199 dataset, I analyzed structural MRI scans from 170 subjects (85 FCD patients and 85 healthy controls) using both T1-weighted tissue segmentation and FLAIR imaging.

The preprocessing pipeline was developed in MATLAB using SPM. FLAIR scans were coregistered into native T1 anatomical space, lesion masks were spatially aligned during reslicing, and tissue probability maps for gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid were generated through segmentation workflows. From these outputs, I extracted whole-brain tissue composition measurements, asymmetry metrics, and high-percentile FLAIR intensity statistics designed to capture subtle structural abnormalities.

I then built a feature-engineered machine learning framework in Python using logistic regression with stratified five-fold cross-validation. The project emphasized interpretability rather than black-box prediction, so leakage-prone variables such as lesion size and mask availability were explicitly removed before training. The final models achieved cross-validated ROC-AUC values near 0.71 using segmentation-derived structural features and global FLAIR measurements.

Beyond classification performance, the project also explored lesion-specific structural characteristics. Lesion regions consistently demonstrated elevated FLAIR intensity relative to surrounding tissue, while segmentation overlap analysis showed that lesion voxels were composed primarily of gray matter probability mass. These findings supported the hypothesis that interpretable multimodal MRI features can capture meaningful structural signatures of focal cortical dysplasia at both the global and lesion-specific level.
